questions.q: A particle executes S.H.M. of amplitude $A$~along $x$-axis. At $t = 0$, the position of the particle is $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ and it moves along positive $x$-axis. The displacement of particle in time $t$ is $x = Asin \left(\omegat + \delta\right),$then the value \delta will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f ( x ) = e^{x}\sin x$

We know that the slope of tangent is given by~\left\{\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f^{'}\left(x\right)\right\}$.

Now,

$f^{'} ( x ) = Z = e^{x}\sin x + e^{x}\cos x$

$Z = e^{x} \left(\sin x + \cos x\right)$

\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$e^{x} \left(\sin x + \cos x\right) + e^{x} \left(\cos x - \sin x\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$2e^{x}\cos x$

For maxima,~\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$0$

$⇒ 2e^{x}\cos x = 0$

$⇒ e^{x}\cos x = 0$

$∵ e^{x} \ne 0, x \in R$~

$∴ \cos x = 0 ⇒ x = $\dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$; \left\{∵ x \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]\right\}$

Now,~

$⇒ $\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}} =$2e^{x}\cos x - 2e^{x}\sin x$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } $= 2e^{x} \left($\cos x - \sin x\right)$

\left\${\left(\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}}\right)$x = $\dfrac{π}{2}= $-2e\dfrac{π}{2}< 0 \to \text{MAXIMA}$

And,~\left\{\left(\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right\} = 2e\dfrac{3\pi}{2} > 0 \to \text{MINIMA}$

Hence,~$Z = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \left(\text{slope of tangent}\right)~is maximum when~$x = \dfrac{π}{2}.$

questions.q: The time period of oscillation of a simple pendulum of length $L$~suspended from the roof of a vehicle, which moves without friction down an inclined plane of inclination $\alpha$, is given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration of vehicle down the incline will be $a = gsin\alpha$
In the frame of the vehicle, we have to apply pseudo force. The Force diagram is shown in figure.
Component of $mg$~along the inclined (i.e. $mgsin\alpha$)~will balance the pseudo force. Therefore,~${g}_{eff} = g cos \alpha$


Hence,

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{geff}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g cos \alpha}}$.

questions.q: A pendulum is executing simple harmonic motion and its maximum kinetic energy is $\mathrm{K}_{1}$. If the length of the pendulum is doubled and it performs simple harmonic motion with the same amplitude as in the first case, its maximum kinetic energy is $\mathrm{K}_{2}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $K=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} x^{2}\Rightarrow K_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^{2} A^{2}$ A $=L \theta\omega=\sqrt{\frac{g}{L}}\Rightarrow K=\frac{1}{2} m \cdot \frac{g}{L} \cdot L^{2} \theta^{2}=\frac{1}{2} m g L \theta^{2}\therefore \frac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}=\frac{L}{2 L}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow K_{2}=2 K_{1}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{K}_{1}}{\mathrm{~K}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{L}}{2 \mathrm{~L}}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}_{2}=2 \mathrm{~K}_{1}$

questions.q: The point $A$~moves with a uniform speed along the circumference of a circle of radius $0 . 36m$ and covers $30 °$ in $0 . 1s$. The perpendicular projection $P$ from $A$ on the diameter $MN$ represents the simple harmonic motion of $P$. The restoration force per unit mass when $P$ touches $M$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The point $A$ covers $30 °$ in $0 . 1s$.
Then, we have~$\dfrac{π}{6}rad ⟶ 0 . 1s$.
Or~$1rad ⟶ \dfrac{0 . 1}{\dfrac{π}{6}}s$
Or~$2\pi in \to \dfrac{0 . 1 \times 6}{π} \times 2\pi$
Thus, time taken is~$T = 1 . 2sec .$

We know that $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$
Then,~$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{1 . 2}$
Restoration force $( F ) = {mω}^{2}A .$

Then Restoration force per unit mass \left(\dfrac{F}{m}\right) = {ω}^{2}A$
\left(\dfrac{F}{m}\right) = \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{1 . 2}\right)2 \times 0 . 36$

$≅ 9 . 87N$

questions.q: A cylindrical plastic bottle of negligible mass is filled with $310ml$ of water and left floating in a pond with still water. If pressed downward slightly and released, it starts performing simple harmonic motion at angular frequency $\omega .$ If the radius of the bottle is $2.5$ cm then $\omega$ is close to: $($ density of water $= {10}^{3}kg / m^{3} )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let at equilibrium, $y$ length of bottle is immerged in water:

So, $mg = {f}_{buo}$

$mg = ρ\left(Ay\right)g$ ..... $( 1 )$ [Equilibrium Condition]

Now it is further pushed by distance $x$

${F}_{restoring} = ρ [ A\left(x + y )\right]g - mg$

$m{\omega}^{2}x = ρAxg + ρAyg - mg$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{ρAg}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{ρAg}{ρV}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\pir^{2}g}{V}} =7.9 rad / sec$

questions.q: A block of mass m attached to a massless spring is performing oscillatory motion of amplitude 'A' on a frictionless horizontal plane. If half of the mass of the block breaks off when it is passing through its equilibrium point, the amplitude of oscillation for the remaining system become ƒA. The value of ƒ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using mometum conservation&

${m}_{1}{v}_{1} = {m}_{2}{v}_{2}mA\omega = \dfrac{m}{2}{A}_{2}{ω}_{2}mA\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} = \dfrac{m}{2}{A}_{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m / 2}}{A}_{2} = \sqrt{2}A ⇒ f = \sqrt{2}$

From phasor,

$\begin{aligned} & \phi=\tan ^{-1} \frac{2 \sqrt{7} \times \sqrt{3} / 2}{\sqrt{7}+2 \sqrt{7} \times \frac{1}{2}}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{21}}{2 \sqrt{7}}=\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{R}}=7 \sin (5 \mathrm{t}+\phi) \\ & \quad \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{R}}=-7 \times 25 \sin (5 \mathrm{t}+\phi) \\ & \therefore \mathrm{a}_{\max }=175 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm\sec=175 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm\sec\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The displacement of a damped harmonic oscillator is given by $x\left(t\right) = e^{- 0.1t}\cos \left(10\pit + \phi\right) .$ Here $t$ is in seconds. The time taken for its amplitude of vibration to drop to half of its initial value is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Amplitude $A = {A}_{0}e^{- kt}$
From given condition, $\dfrac{{A}_{0}}{2} = {A}_{0}e^{- 0.1 \times t}$
$⇒ \ln 2 = 0.1 \times t$
$t = \dfrac{\ln 2}{0.1} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.10} = 6.935 \approx 7s$

questions.q: Choose the correct length $( L )$~versus square of time period $( {T}_{2} )$ ) graph for a simple pendulum executing simple harmonic motion.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A simple pendulum consists of a point mass attached to an inextensible string and suspended from a support.

The formula to calculate the time period& \left(T\right)$~of a simple pendulum is given by

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where,~$l$~is the length of the pendulum and~$g$~is the acceleration due to gravity.

Simplify equation (1) to obtain the relation between the time period and the length.

$\begin{cases}T^{2} & = & \dfrac{4{π}^{2}}{g} \times 퓁 \\ T^{2} & ∝ & l . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 2 )\end{cases}$

Equation (2) suggests that the graph between the square of the time period versus the length of the pendulum is a straight line passing through the origin.

$

questions.q: In figure (A), mass $2m$~is fixed on mass $m$~which is attached to two springs of spring constant $k$. In figure (B), mass $m$~is attached to two spring of spring constant $k$~and $2k$. If mass $m$~in (A) and (B) are displaced by distance $x$~horizontally and then released, then time period ${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{2}$ corresponding to (A) and (B) respectively follow the relation.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time period of spring block system is given by& $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$.

In both the cases springs are connected in parallel,

In case $1$:~${k}_{eq} = 2k$~and total mass is~$3m$. Therefore,

~${T}_{1} = 2\pi\sqrt{\left(3m\right){k}_{eq}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\left(3m\right)2k}$

In case~$2:{k}_{eq} = 3k$~and total mass is $m$. Therefore,

${T}_{2} = 2\pi\sqrt{\left(m\right)3k}$

$⇒ \dfrac{T1}{T2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: Which graph represents the difference between total energy and potential energy of a particle executing $SHM$& vs its distance from mean position?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In a SHM, mechanical energy is conserved. So, the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy remains constant.

For a SHM,

$T . E . - U = K . E$

$⇒ T . E . - U = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2} \left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right)

This is the equation of a downward parabola.

$

questions.q: In the given figure, a body of mass $M$ is held between two massless springs, on a smooth inclined plane. The free ends of the springs are attached to firm supports. If each spring has spring constant $k,$ the frequency of oscillation of given body is:

questions.solution:
${K}_{eq} = {K}_{1} + {K}_{2} = K + K = 2K$

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{Keq}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2K}}$

$f = \dfrac{1}{T} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{2K}{m}}$

questions.q: A block of mass $1$ kg attached to a spring is made to oscillate with an initial amplitude of $12$ cm. After $2$ minutes the amplitude decreases to $6$ cm. Determine the value of the damping constant for this motion. (take $\ln 2 = 0 . 693$& )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The amplitude of damped oscillation with time& $t$~and damping constant~$b$~is given by,

$A = {A}_{0}e^{- bt / 2m}$

$⇒ \ln \left(\dfrac{A0}{A}\right) = \dfrac{bt}{2m}$

$⇒ \ln 2 = \dfrac{b}{2m} \times 120$; here~$t = 2min = 120s$

$⇒ \dfrac{0 . 693 \times 2 \times 1}{120} = b$

$⇒ b = 1 . 16 \times {10}^{- 2}kgs^{- 1}$.

questions.q:
Time period of a simple pendulum in a stationary lift is $T$. If the lift accelerates with $\dfrac{g}{6}$ vertically upwards then the time period will be
(Where $g =$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

In an upward accelerating frame the effective~${g}_{eff} = g + a$

$⇒ {T}_{2} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g + a}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g + \dfrac{g}{6}}}$

$\dfrac{T}{T2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g + \dfrac{g}{6}}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{6}}$

$⇒ {T}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6}{7}}T$

questions.q: A body is performing simple harmonic with an amplitude of $10$ cm. The velocity of the body was tripled by air Jet when it is at $5$ cm from its mean position. The new amplitude of vibration is $\sqrt{x}cm$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In SHM, velocity of the particle at any displacement,& $x$~is given by,~$v = \sqrt{A^{2} - x^{2}}$.

Therefore,

$⇒ \dfrac{v}{3v} = \left(\sqrt{{A}_{1}^{2} - 25}\right)\sqrt{{A}_{2}^{2} - 25}⇒ \sqrt{{A}_{2}^{2} - 25} = 3 \times \sqrt{75}$

$⇒ {A}_{2}^{2} = 700⇒ {A}_{2} = \sqrt{700}cm$

questions.q:
A simple pendulum is placed at a place where its distance from the earth's surface is equal to the radius of the earth. If the length of the string is $4m$, then the time period of small oscillations will be _________s$.

$[$take $g = {π}^{2}ms^{- 2}]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at surface of earth, $g = \dfrac{GM}{R2}$.

Now, at distance $R$ from the surface of the earth, $g^{'} = \dfrac{GM}{\left(R + R\right)2} = \dfrac{g}{4}$

Therefore,
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\dfrac{g}{4}}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 4}{g}}$

$⇒ T = 2\pi\dfrac{4}{π} = 8s$

questions.q: At a given point of time the value of displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is given as& $y = Acos\left(30 °\right) .$ If amplitude is $40$ cm and kinetic energy at that time is $200J,$~the value of force constant $1 . 0 \times {10}^{x}Nm^{– 1}$. The value of~$x$& is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the kinetic energy& \left(K\right)$~of a particle executing SHM is given by

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}k \left(A^{2} - y^{2}\right) . . . \left($1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of the unknown parameter.

$\begin{cases}K \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2} \timesk \times \left(A^{2} - A^{2}\cos^{2}30 °\right) \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2} \timesk \timesA^{2}\sin^{2}30 ° \\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } 200 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times1 . 0 \times {10}^{x} \times \left(0 . 4\right)2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{x}}{100}\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } {10}^{2} = {10}^{x - 2} \\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } x - 2 = 2 \\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } x = 4\end{cases}$$

$

questions.q: A particle of mass $250g$~executes a simple harmonic motion under a periodic force $F = ( – 25x ) N$. The particle attains a maximum speed of $4ms^{- 1}$ during its oscillation. The amplitude of the motion is ______cm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, force& $F = ( – 25x ) N$

$⇒ 0 . 25a = - 25x$

$⇒ a = - 100x$

Now comparing it with standard equation,~$a = - {ω}^{2}x$~we get

$\omega = 10$.

Now,~${v}_\max = \omegaA$

$⇒ \omegaA = 4$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{4}{10} = 0 . 4m$

$⇒ A = 40cm$.
